rows.name: SLICE_REPO_ROOT

problems.statement: Inside a Dice grant, `bin/slice run` and `bin/slice bench` read `resource-parser.sh` and `resource-map.yaml` from `/opt/positron/config`.
problems.code_says: Inside a grant only the lookups that pass deployed_resources (slot count fallback, NUMA mapping, FPGA devices of an instance) use /opt/positron/config. get_server_type() is called without that argument in cmd_run and in the benchmark file helpers, so the server type still comes from <root>/config.

cells.Set by: Slice test fixtures. A person can set it by hand.
cells.Values and default: Path of a directory with the layout of the repository root. Unset: the parent directory of the `bin` directory that holds the `bin/slice` script.
cells.Effect: Changes where `bin/slice` finds `config/test-benchmarks.json`, `config/resource-parser.sh`, `config/resource-map.yaml`, `gen/` and `bin/dice`. `bin/slice` also writes its `logs-<host>` directory there. With `--remote`, a value that names a directory other than the checkout of the script ends `bin/slice` with an error and exit status 2. Inside a Dice grant, `bin/slice run` and `bin/slice bench` read the FPGA cards and NUMA nodes of the slots from `resource-parser.sh` and `resource-map.yaml` in `/opt/positron/config`. They still read the server type from the `config` files under this directory.

rows.name: DICE_ETA

cells.Values and default: Seconds as a number of 0 or more, or `inf`, `infinity`, `infty`, or `?` for no estimate. A negative number or other text makes `slice submit` exit with status 2. Unset: `inf`. Dice then expects no end time for the submission.
cells.Effect: Sets the predicted run time that the wrapper passes as `--eta` to `bin/slice submit` when it queues `rinzler` or `runtron` through Dice. The Dice scheduler uses the value to decide whether a later submission can start before an earlier one. The wrapper reads it only on a shared host outside a grant. Dice does not stop a submission that runs longer. `bin/dice-lsf-runner` removes every `DICE_` variable from remote work. A value from the submitting shell does not reach a `--remote` run.

rows.name: MAX_TOKENS_BASE

problems.statement: The script header says that long prompt mode needs a server context window of `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX` plus base plus jitter tokens.
problems.code_says: Style only: the sentence reports a source comment. The code shows the behavior: the script sends up to PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX estimated prompt tokens and an explicit max_tokens of up to base plus jitter, and rinzler answers HTTP 400 when prompt tokens plus explicit max_tokens exceed the total limit.

cells.Values and default: Whole number of tokens from `1` to `999999999`, without a leading zero. It must be larger than `MAX_TOKENS_JITTER`. Any other value stops the script with exit status 1. Unset: 512 tokens.
cells.Effect: It is the middle of the `max_tokens` range of `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server). Each request gets a random `max_tokens` from base minus jitter to base plus jitter. The option `-t` or `--max-tokens` overrides the variable. When `PROMPT_MODE` is `long`, a request can hold up to `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX` estimated prompt tokens and a `max_tokens` of up to base plus jitter. `rinzler` rejects a request with HTTP status 400 when its prompt tokens plus `max_tokens` exceed the context length of the model.

evidence: perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:26 - MAX_TOKENS_BASE="${MAX_TOKENS_BASE:-512}"
perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:234 - the value must match ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,8})$, otherwise exit 1
perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:239 - jitter >= base ends the script with exit 1
perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:402 - max_tokens = base - jitter + RANDOM % (2 * jitter + 1)
perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:155 - the options -t and --max-tokens assign MAX_TOKENS_BASE
perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:405 - in long mode the prompt size is drawn up to PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX
src/rinzler/token-limits.cpp:76 - prompt tokens plus explicit max_tokens above the total limit give reject_total
src/rinzler.cpp:3177 - rinzler answers reject_total with HTTP 400

rows.name: MAX_TOKENS_JITTER

cells.Values and default: Whole number of tokens from `0`, without a leading zero. It must be smaller than `MAX_TOKENS_BASE`. Any other value stops the script with exit status 1. Unset: 128 tokens.
cells.Effect: It is half of the width of the random `max_tokens` range of `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server). Each request gets a `max_tokens` from base minus jitter to base plus jitter. The value `0` gives every request the base value. The option `-j` or `--jitter` overrides the variable. Above 16383 tokens the range ends below base plus jitter. The bash variable `RANDOM` gives at most 32767.

evidence: perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:27 - MAX_TOKENS_JITTER="${MAX_TOKENS_JITTER:-128}"
perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:234 - the value must match ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,8})$, otherwise exit 1
perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:239 - jitter >= base ends the script with exit 1
perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:402 - max_tokens = base - jitter + RANDOM % (2 * jitter + 1); RANDOM is at most 32767, so a jitter above 16383 cannot reach base plus jitter
perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:159 - the options -j and --jitter assign MAX_TOKENS_JITTER

notes:
Twelve rows checked against main at 7eddde7895. Three rows changed: SLICE_REPO_ROOT, SLICE_STATE_DIR and MAX_TOKENS_BASE. Nine rows are unchanged.
SLICE_REPO_ROOT: inside a Dice grant only the lookups that pass deployed_resources use /opt/positron/config. The server type still comes from the config files under the root, because cmd_run and the benchmark file helpers call get_server_type() with its defaults (bin/slice:4226, bin/slice:2040).
SLICE_STATE_DIR: only the run path writes a state file (bin/slice:4530). bin/slice bench runs tests and writes none. The word "stale" was replaced as the plain-English hint asked, and the code confirms the meaning (bin/slice:2913).
MAX_TOKENS_BASE: the sentence about the script header was replaced by behavior that the code shows. rinzler answers HTTP 400 when prompt tokens plus an explicit max_tokens exceed the total limit, which is the smaller of the server total limit and the model context length (src/rinzler/token-limits.cpp:76, src/rinzler.cpp:3177). The PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX row of another chunk holds the same kind of sentence ("The script header says ...") and can use the same replacement.
Not changed, for the next editor to decide: (1) the DICE_ETA cell "Values and default" writes `slice submit` and the "Effect" cell writes `bin/slice submit` for the same command. (2) In table 3.1 the rows API_KEY to MODEL write "The person who runs `burst-test.sh`." in "Set by", and the later rows of the same table write "A developer who runs `burst-test.sh`.". (3) DICE_ETA: `inf` and `?` are different values on the wire, but bin/dice schedules both the same way (neither starts before an earlier submission, bin/dice:1440), so the cell text holds.
The index of the checkout changed during this work, and this check wrote nothing there: at the start it held a staged README.environment.md, and at the end it held a staged README.env-vars.md in its place (AGENTS.md and README.md stay modified). HEAD stayed at 7eddde7895, and the source files cited as evidence have no difference from HEAD. The staged README copies were not used as evidence.
